definition: The high-dimensional surface representing how a model's loss value changes as a function of its parameters, which optimization algorithms navigate during training.
details: Understanding loss landscape geometry — including the presence of local minima, saddle points, and flat versus sharp minima — helps researchers reason about why certain optimization strategies and architectural choices work better than others.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Loss Landscape.
